Title: Using simple models to describe the kinetics of growth, glucose consumption, and monoclonal antibody formation in naive and infliximab producer CHO cells

Abstract: Abstract Despite their practical and commercial relevance, there are few reports on the kinetics of growth and production of Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells—the most frequently used host for the industrial production of therapeutic proteins. We characterize the kinetics of cell growth, substrate consumption, and product formation in naive and monoclonal antibody (mAb) producing recombinant CHO cells. Culture experiments were performed in 125 mL shake flasks on commercial culture medium (CD Opti CHO™ Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA) diluted to different glucose concentrations (1.2–4.8 g/L).

Model: Monod growth with Luedeking-Piret mAb formation (CHO, 33 and 37 C)
Laws:
(1) [balance] Biomass grows at a first-order rate during the initial exponential-growth stage.
(3) [constitutive] A Monod-type specific growth rate depends on substrate concentration adjusted by the minimum concentration at which growth was observed.
(4) [balance] The substrate-consumption balance relates glucose consumption to cell growth through the cell yield coefficient.
(5) [balance] The mAb production rate combines growth-associated production with production proportional to viable cell concentration.

States (computed by the ODEs):
- [X]: Cell concentration at a given time
- r_{s}: Global rate of glucose consumption
- [P]: mAb concentration at a given point

Inputs (variables no law computes):
- [S]: Substrate concentration in the culture used in the Monod growth law
- r_{x}: Rate of cell growth
- r_{p}: Rate of accumulation of product in time within the reaction vessel

Model-wide assumptions:
- none recorded

answer.description: The model describes naive and infliximab-producing CHO cells in shake-flask culture and predicts cell concentration, glucose consumption, and monoclonal antibody accumulation. Cell growth depends on glucose through a Monod relationship with a minimum growth-supporting concentration, while glucose consumption is linked to growth by a yield coefficient. Antibody formation follows a Luedeking–Piret model with growth-associated and cell-associated contributions.
